A.notes: A is clear and competent, with a solid hero and accurate product mockups, but it feels very close to a standard dark SaaS landing page. The scroll-frame strip shows little motion progression beyond normal section-to-section scrolling, and on mobile the steps/pricing content appears to drop out into large empty gaps, which hurts craft despite strong accessibility and performance checks.

B.notes: B has a much stronger governing idea: the whole page is built around isolating one lit line from a stream, and that idea carries through structure, art direction, and copy. The scroll frames suggest purposeful progression in the how-it-works/product sections, with reduced motion preserving the full content state; I can't judge timing from stills, but the motion appears to serve the story rather than decorate it.

raw.why: B is more distinctive and conceptually unified, with motion and layout choices that better express the product's promise while still passing the accessibility/performance checks.
